paragraphs.en: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun. These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers. Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said, they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.
paragraphs.zh: 启迪人心、富有挑战、激发思考、充满乐趣。这些是《自然》读者在一系列有关艺术家与研究人员合作的文章中，用来描述自身艺术与科学合作体验的一些词语。在参与配套调查的大约350人中，近40%表示自己曾与艺术家合作；几乎所有人都说，未来会考虑开展这样的合作。

paragraphs.en: Such an encouraging result is not surprising. Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them communicate their work to new audiences. “Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning,” one respondent said.
paragraphs.zh: 这样令人鼓舞的结果并不意外。科学家正越来越多地寻找视觉艺术家，帮助他们向新的受众传播研究成果。一位受访者说：“艺术家帮助科学家接触更广泛的受众，并建立促进学习的情感联系。”

paragraphs.en: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the scenes came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons. They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University’s Climate Change Communication Research Hub. The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November’s United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK.
paragraphs.zh: 艺术家和科学家如何携手带来轰动效应，上个月就有一个例子：悉尼交响乐团演奏了安东尼奥·维瓦尔第《四季》的改编版本。他们把莫纳什大学气候变化传播研究中心提供的各季节最新气候预测数据融入乐谱，对这份已有300年历史的作品进行了重新构想。这场演出以富有创意的形式呼吁人们采取行动，为11月将在英国格拉斯哥举行的联合国气候变化大会预热。

paragraphs.en: But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street. Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll, however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements. Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study. The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other’s work. Such an approach can both prompt new research as well as result in powerful art.
paragraphs.zh: 但真正的合作必须是双向的。回应《自然》调查的艺术家少于科学家，不过，一些受访者指出，艺术家并不只是帮助科学家满足传播需求，艺术家的作品也不应仅被看作研究对象。当科学家与艺术家在项目中拥有共同的关切，能够共同设计项目，并能对彼此的工作提出批评时，这种合作最有价值。这样的方式既能催生新的研究，也能产生具有强大感染力的艺术作品。

paragraphs.en: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture. The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the “visual studies” in the name. Light was a something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration. As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.
paragraphs.zh: 半个多世纪以前，麻省理工学院成立了高级视觉研究中心（CAVS），探索技术在文化中的作用。创始人有意让各个项目围绕光展开，因此该中心的名称中才有“视觉研究”。光是艺术家和科学家都感兴趣的事物，因而能够成为合作的基础。随着科学技术不断进步，并细分为更多分支学科，该中心同时也在展望这样一个时代：顶尖研究人员也可以是艺术家、作家和诗人，而后者也可以成为顶尖研究人员。

paragraphs.en: Nature’s poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, tomake a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time, and embrace surprise and challenge. The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other. Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.
paragraphs.zh: 《自然》的调查结果表明，这一趋势一如既往地强劲，但要让合作取得成效，双方都需要投入时间，并乐于接受意外与挑战。艺术与科学合作的范围需要超越研究成果传播这一必要目的，参与者也必须避免陷入对彼此抱有刻板印象的陷阱。艺术家和科学家都致力于发现与创造，挑战与批评也都是两者的核心。
